content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) has established a risk categorization system for foot health in diabetic patients, which determines the frequency of foot examinations based on the level of risk: Category 0: This category represents individuals at very low risk. These patients do not exhibit Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS) or Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD). They should undergo a foot examination annually. Category 1: Patients in this category are considered at low risk. They present with either LOPS or PAD. Foot examinations are recommended every 6 to 12 months. Category 2: This category includes patients at moderate risk. These individuals have both LOPS and PAD, or they exhibit foot deformities. They should have their feet examined every 3 to 6 months. Category 3: Patients in this category are at high risk. They have a history of foot ulcers or have undergone amputation. These individuals require foot examinations every 1 to 3 months.
